column1: # Notice boards as actually seen in game.  EDIT ME.
# One row per board entry, so a single sighting is several rows sharing a
# `seen` and a `port`.  Nothing here is generated - it is field notes, and it
# is the only file in the project that records what the game really does
# rather than what we assume it does.
#   seen     when you looked, to the minute.  Local time is fine, but be
#            consistent: the 00:00 UTC daily reset is one of the things these
#            notes are meant to pin down.
#   port     the port whose board you are reading.
#   kind     courier | bounty
#   entry    courier: `origin > destination`, the two ports as the board shows
#            them.  bounty: the creature.  Shorthand is fine - the ports are
#            resolvable against the task pool later, and the board itself is
#            always one of the two ends.
#   cargo    courier only, and optional - but it is what makes an entry
#            unambiguous.  `The Summer Shore > The Pandemonium` matches two
#            different tasks (Coral x2 and Sea shells x3); the cargo picks one.
#   shade    how the entry was coloured, as an ordinal, because there turn out
#            to be at least two distinct highlights:
#              plain  the same as everything else on the board
#              hi1    the usual highlight (albatross, at Summer Shore and
#                     Port Roberts)
#              hi2    darker still than hi1 (frigatebird, at Civitas)
#            Every board so far carries exactly one non-plain entry, and it is
#            always a bounty - which is what the wiki's "one bounty task that
#            will always be available" would look like.  What separates hi1
#            from hi2 is open: it is not simply bird versus fish, since osprey
#            sat plain on the same board where frigatebird was hi2.
#   note     anything else.  Worth recording: how many deliveries you had done
#            since the last reroll, and whether the board had changed since you
#            last saw it.
# What these notes are for, in rough order of how much they matter:
#   1. How many entries a board shows, and the courier/bounty split.  We assume
#      4 courier tasks; the first sighting below shows 5 courier and 3 bounty,
#      so the assumption is already suspect.
#   2. Whether the highlighted entry is the guaranteed bounty.
#   3. Whether courier entries ever fall outside the pool we think a board has
#      - if one does, port_tasks.list is incomplete.
#   4. What the second highlight shade means.
#   5. Whether the reroll really is 8 completions, which the wiki flags as
#      unconfirmed.
seen
